title: Argumentation labor
theory: Toulmin's (1958) model of argument, with argumentation labor: the largely invisible work people do to rebuild, test, weigh or complete an argument when part of it breaks down, in four kinds (reconstructive, comparative, adjudicative, integrative), as theorized in prior work on AI-augmented radiology.
about: A coding lens: it adds a layer to the map that the researcher or the model codes while reading the note. Switch it off when your study does not use this theory; the workflow and claims layers stand on their own.

toulmin.claim: The conclusion asserted (a finding, a diagnosis, a fix).
toulmin.data: The evidence the claim rests on.
toulmin.warrant: Why the data supports the claim.
toulmin.backing: What makes the warrant trustworthy (for an AI, how it was validated or trained).
toulmin.qualifier: How strongly the claim is held (priority, confidence).
toulmin.rebuttal: Conditions under which the claim would not hold.

argument_status.missing: The element is not given at all (e.g. a flag with no reason).
argument_status.ambiguous: The element is given but can be read more than one way.
argument_status.opaque: The element exists but cannot be inspected.
argument_status.absent: The reader would expect it and it is not there.
argument_status.unstable: The element changes over time or between cases (e.g. after a model update).
argument_status.expanded: The reader adds more of this element than usual (e.g. extra rebuttals).
argument_status.persistent: The element stays open after sign-off (e.g. a rebuttal carried into the report).

labor.C: Comparative: testing own judgment against the machine, case by case
labor.A: Adjudicative: deciding to trust or dismiss under false flags, drift, alerts
labor.I: Integrative: synthesising machine output with history, physiology, trajectory

rules: Code a breakdown only where the note shows one; an empty list is a valid answer.
Every breakdown names one Toulmin element, one status and at least one kind of labor.
The same labor codes may also be put on the steps where that labor happens.
